statements.t: Based on these solid results and the dramatic improvements we have made across the key capabilities required to win in our industry, we are raising our full year sales outlook and now expect to deliver positive sales growth in both the fourth quarter and full year 2026."

Mark Erceg, Newell Brands Chief Financial Officer, said, "Stronger sales and world-class productivity efforts allowed third quarter normalized gross and operating margins to expand significantly versus last year and normalized earnings per share to come in at the high end of our guidance range despite inflation that exceeded our expectations.

Higher projected sales than previously anticipated and additional cost containment efforts give us the confidence to maintain the midpoints of our normalized operating margin and normalized earnings per share outlooks.
Deleveraging remains a top priority and, consistent with that, we anticipate reducing total debt and factoring by a couple hundred million dollars this year."
The Company initiated its outlook for the fourth quarter and raised its full-year 2026 sales outlook, reflecting third-quarter performance and updated expectations for the fourth quarter.

The Company revised its full-year 2026 operating cash flow outlook primarily due to two one-time non-operating items, the first of which relates to the previously announced termination of its non-qualified defined benefit plans.
The second item reflects lower than previously anticipated proceeds from receivables factoring as the Company reduces its reliance on these programs following its upsized bond refinancing.
Based on these two items the Company has revised its full-year operating cash flow guidance to approximately $150 million.
A webcast replay will be made available in the Quarterly Earnings section of the Company’s website.
